source_text: ἐπαίνου παντὸς διᾴττειν ἤδη πως τόν γε τοιοῦτον ἐρεῖς; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Καὶ μάλα. {ΚΥΡ.} Τί δὲ, οὐχὶ τὸ ξυρᾶσθαι καὶ καταψιλοῦσθαι τὴν κεφαλὴν τεμνομένης ἐν Χριστῷ [γρ. Χρωτὶ] τῆς τριχὸς, ἀτιμίας ὑπόληψιν ἐργάσαιτ' ἂν, οἷσπερ ἂν ὅλως συμβαίνοι τυχὸν, ἰέναι; {ΠΑΛΛ.} Συνίημι. {ΚΥΡ.} Εἰ γὰρ Θεοῦ λέγοντος πρὸς τὴν τῶν Ἰουδαίων μητέρα, φημὶ δὲ τὴν Ἱερουσαλὴμ, «Ξύρησαι καὶ κεῖρε ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα τὰ τρυφερά σου. Ἐμπλάτυνον τὴν χηρείαν σου ὡς ἀετὸς, ὅτι ᾐχμαλωτεύθησαν ἀπὸ σοῦ.» Ὑβρίστρια γὰρ καὶ ἀτιμοποιὸς ἡ ξύρησις, καὶ τοῖς πενθοῦσι πρεπωδεστάτη. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Εὖ ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Γυμνὸς οὖν ἄρα καὶ ἀτιμότατος νοῦς, καὶ αἰσχύνης ἔμπλεως οὐκ ἔχων ἐν ἑαυτῷ τὰ δι' ὧν θαυμάζεται. Εἶεν δ' ἂν ἐν τούτοις καὶ μάλα εἰκότως οἵ τε ὀλιγογνώμονες, καὶ παρεφθαρμένην ἔχοντες ἐπὶ Θεῷ τὴν δόξαν, ὡς λίθοις προσκυνεῖν, ἤγουν ἀσυνέτως ἀποτολμᾷν ἀπονέμειν τῇ κτίσει τὸ σέβας, παρὰ τὸν κτίστην καὶ ποιητὴν, καὶ τὰ εἰσάπαν διεστραμμένα φρονεῖν τε καὶ λέγειν, καὶ τὴν μὲν ἀληθῆ καὶ ἀμώμητον ἀποσείεσθαι πίστιν, ἐπιθρώσκειν δὲ μᾶλλον, οἷς ἂν ἐξ ἠλιθιότητος παραφθέγξαιτό τις, διάτοι τὸν νοῦν ἀγαθοῖς οὐκ ἔχειν κατακομῶντα λογισμοῖς. {ΠΑΛΛ.} Ἄριστα ἔφης. {ΚΥΡ.} Ἔστω δὴ οὖν τοῖς εἰς ὀρθότητα λογισμοῖς μεμεστωμένος ὁ νοῦς, καὶ ἐννοιῶν εὑρήμασι τοῖς εἰς πᾶν ὁτιοῦν τῶν τεθαυμασμένων, οἷά τινι κόμῃ κατεστεμμένος. Ἔμφρων γὰρ ὁ τοιοῦτός ἐστιν ὅτι μάλιστά γε, καὶ ἐπιτηδείως ἔχων εἴς γε τὸ χρῆναι λοιπὸν τὸν ἐν Χριστῷ διὰ πίστεως εἰσοικίσασθαι φωτισμόν. Εὐφυᾶ δὲ οὕτω καὶ ἀπόλεκτον ἐξησκηκότα ζωὴν, τὸν νῷ τοιῷδε διαπρεπῆ, παντὸς τοῦ καταμιαίνειν πεφυκότος οἴχεσθαι μακρὰν τὸ θεῖον ἡμῖν ἐπιτάττει χρησμῴδημα, καὶ σαρκικῶν μὲν ἔργων ἀποχωρεῖν, τὰ δὲ ὅσα βλέπει πρὸς νέκρωσιν καὶ φθορὰν, ὡς ἀπωτάτω ῥίπτειν. Τοιγάρτοι μὴ χρῆναι τοῖς τεθνεῶσιν ἐπιφοιτᾷν, μήτε μὴν ἐπὶ νεκρῷ καταμιαίνεσθαι φιλεῖν, τοῦτό που πάντως ἡμῖν ὑπαινίττεται. Ἐξείργει δὲ τοῦ τοιοῦδε παντελῶς ὁ νόμος, καὶ τῆς εἰς γονέας αἰδοῦς ἄμεινον τιθεὶς τὸ τῷ Θεῷ δοκοῦν. «Ἐπὶ πατρὶ γὰρ, φησὶ, καὶ ἐπὶ μητρὶ οὐκ εἰσελεύσεται.» Κατορθουμένης γὰρ ἀρετῆς, ἐῤῥέτω φιλοσαρκία, τῆς ἐξ αἵματος οἰκειότητος ἐν λόγῳ τῷ προὔχοντι καὶ ἀμείνονι ἔστω Θεός. Τοῦτό τοι καὶ αὐτὸς ἔφασκεν ὁ Χριστός· «Ὁ φιλῶν πατέρα ἢ μητέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος, καὶ ὁ φιλῶν υἱὸν ἢ θυγατέρα ὑπὲρ ἐμὲ, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος. Καὶ ὃς οὐ λαμβάνει τὸν σταυρὸν αὐτοῦ, καὶ ἀκολουθεῖ ὀπίσω μου, οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος.» Ὅτι δὲ τὰ Θεοῦ, τῆς εἰς γονέας αἰδοῦς ἐν ἀμείνοσι, καὶ αὐτὸς ἡμᾶς ἐδίδαξεν ὁ Σωτήρ. Προσῄει μὲν γάρ τις τῶν ἤδη τελούντων
pass_a_gloss: CYR. [cont.]: ...of every praise (ἔπαινος)? PALL.: Very much. CYR.: And what: will not being shaved (ξυράομαι) and stripped bare (καταψιλόομαι) on the head, the hair being cut to the skin (ἐν χρωτί; print 'ἐν Χριστῷ' with marginal γρ. Χρωτί), work a supposition (ὑπόληψις) of dishonor (ἀτιμία) for whomever it might perhaps happen (συμβαίνω) to come to? PALL.: I understand (συνίημι). CYR.: For if, God saying to the mother of the Jews, I mean Jerusalem: [Micah 1:16 LXX] shave and shear (κείρω) for your delicate (τρυφερός) children; broaden (ἐμπλατύνω) your widowhood (χηρεία) as an eagle, for they were taken captive (αἰχμαλωτεύω) from you [anacoluthon] — for insulting (ὑβρίστρια) and dishonor-making (ἀτιμοποιός) the shaving (ξύρησις), and most fitting for mourners. PALL.: Well said. CYR.: Naked then and most dishonored the mind (νοῦς), and full of shame (αἰσχύνη), not having in itself the things through which it is wondered at. Among these reasonably would be the small-minded (ὀλιγογνώμονες) and those having a corrupted (παραφθείρω) opinion (δόξα) about God, so as to worship (προσκυνέω) stones, that is (ἤγουν), senselessly (ἀσυνέτως) to dare to apportion reverence (σέβας) to the creation (κτίσις) beside/instead of (παρά) the Creator (κτίστης) and Maker (ποιητής) [Romans 1:25], and to think and say things wholly twisted (διαστρέφω), and to shake off (ἀποσείομαι) the true and blameless faith (πίστις), but rather to leap upon (ἐπιθρώσκω) whatever someone might mis-utter (παραφθέγγομαι) from silliness (ἠλιθιότης), because of not having the mind thick-haired (κατακομάω) with good reasonings (λογισμοί). PALL.: Best said. CYR.: Let the mind be filled (μεστόω) with reasonings toward rightness (ὀρθότης), and crowned (καταστέφω) as with a hair by findings (εὑρήματα) of thoughts toward every admired thing. For such a one is sensible (ἔμφρων) as much as can be, and fitly disposed (ἐπιτηδείως ἔχων) to house within (εἰσοικίζομαι) the enlightenment (φωτισμός) in Christ through faith. The one so naturally gifted (εὐφυής), who has practised (ἐξασκέω) a choice (ἀπόλεκτος) life, distinguished (διαπρεπής) by such mind, the divine oracle (χρησμῴδημα) commands to go far from everything apt by nature to defile (καταμιαίνω), and to withdraw from fleshly works (σαρκικὰ ἔργα), and to cast as far as possible whatever looks to deadness (νέκρωσις) and corruption (φθορά). Therefore the not needing to visit (ἐπιφοιτάω) the dead, nor to love (φιλέω) being defiled over a corpse (νεκρός) — this it surely hints (ὑπαινίττομαι). The law bars from such entirely, setting what seems good to God better than reverence (αἰδώς) toward parents (γονεῖς): [Numbers 6:6–7] upon father and upon mother he shall not go in. For virtue (ἀρετή) being achieved (κατορθόω), let love of flesh (φιλοσαρκία) be gone (ἐρρέτω); in the prior and better account (λόγος) than blood kinship (οἰκειότης) let God be. This Christ himself said: [Matthew 10:37–38] who loves father or mother above (ὑπέρ) me is not worthy (ἄξιος) of me, who loves son or daughter above me is not worthy of me; who does not take (λαμβάνω) his cross (σταυρός) and follow after me is not worthy of me. That the things of God are among the better than reverence toward parents, the Savior (Σωτήρ) himself taught. For there came (πρόσειμι) one of those already ranked (τελέω ἐν) [§21: among the disciples]...
pass_b_english: Cyril: And what of this? Would not shaving and stripping the head bare, with the hair cut close to the skin, bring an impression of dishonor on anyone to whom it might happen?

Cyril: For if God says to the mother of the Jews, I mean Jerusalem, ‘Shave and shear yourself for your delicate children; make your widowhood wide like an eagle, because they have been taken captive from you’ (Micah 1:16), it is because shaving brings insult and dishonor, and is most fitting for those who mourn.

Cyril: Bare, then, and utterly dishonored, and full of shame is the mind that does not have within itself the things that make it admirable. Among such would quite rightly be counted those of little understanding, and those who hold a corrupt opinion of God, so as to worship stones, that is, to dare senselessly to give reverence to the creation rather than to the Creator and Maker (Romans 1:25), and to think and say what is wholly perverse, and to shake off the true and blameless faith, and instead to leap at whatever anyone might blurt out in folly, because their mind has no full head of good thoughts.

Cyril: Let the mind, then, be filled with thoughts that lead to rightness, and be crowned, as with a head of hair, with the discoveries of reflection on everything admirable. Such a person is as sensible as can be, and well fitted from now on to receive into himself the enlightenment that is in Christ through faith. As for the one so well endowed, who has trained himself in an exceptional life and is distinguished by such a mind, the divine oracle commands him to keep far from everything that by its nature defiles, to withdraw from fleshly deeds, and to cast as far away as possible whatever tends toward deadness and corruption. So the rule that one must not visit the dead, nor be willing to be defiled over a corpse, surely hints at this for us. The law bars him from such things entirely, setting what pleases God above reverence for parents. ‘For he shall not go near,’ it says, ‘his father or his mother’ (Numbers 6:6–7). For when virtue is being achieved, away with love of the flesh; let God hold the first and higher place over kinship by blood. This is what Christ himself also said: ‘Whoever loves father or mother more than me is not worthy of me; and whoever loves son or daughter more than me is not worthy of me. And whoever does not take his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me’ (Matthew 10:37–38). The Savior himself also taught us that the things of God rank above reverence for parents. For there came to him one of those already counted…

anf_compare.notes: No public-domain English of De adoratione Book 16. Translated afresh from the PG 68 Greek on 2026-10-23; the withdrawn English was not used for wording.

apparatus.note: PG OCR; a column may cut mid-sentence or mid-word.
The print reads τεμνομένης ἐν Χριστῷ τῆς τριχός; the margin has γρ. χρωτί. The English follows the margin ('cut close to the skin').

Opens with the end of the question begun in §19 ('the portion of all praise?'). The print reads 'τεμνομένης ἐν Χριστῷ τῆς τριχός' with the marginal correction γρ. Χρωτί; 'ἐν Χριστῷ' makes no sense here and 'ἐν χρωτί' is the idiom for cutting close to the skin, so the correction is followed. Micah 1:16 LXX verified (ξύρησαι καὶ κεῖραι ἐπὶ τὰ τέκνα τὰ τρυφερά σου, ἐμπλάτυνον τὴν χηρείαν σου ὡς ἀετός). The 'For if God says…' sentence has no main clause in the Greek; English supplies 'it is because' to join it to the next sentence. 'παρὰ τὸν κτίστην' follows Romans 1:25 (τῇ κτίσει παρὰ τὸν κτίσαντα), a clear allusion. Numbers 6:6–7 cited for 'He shall not go in… to a father or to a mother'. Matthew 10:37–38 verified; Cyril has 'ὁ φιλῶν… ὑπὲρ ἐμέ' and 'λαμβάνει'. 'σαρκικῶν ἔργων' rendered 'fleshly works' and left uncited: it is not the wording of Galatians 5:19. φωτισμός ('enlightenment') may carry a baptismal sense. Last sentence breaks at 'τῶν ἤδη τελούντων'; 'among the disciples' continues in §21.
